decisions.reason: As a bread close to the core assortment that remained visible after launch and shows no clear sign of failure, management would likely continue it because the modest sunk effort is backed by acceptable strategic fit.

This sweet pastry sits near the firm's traditional offer and was still presented after launch, so without strong evidence of disappointment management would tend to retain it rather than admit a mistaken introduction.
Although newer and less publicly emphasized, this farmhouse bread is highly consistent with the bakery's established business, making continued offering more likely than an early withdrawal.
The poppy seed Christmas stollen was publicly highlighted as a flagship and carried a gold-award message, so high visibility and commitment strongly favor persistence.
The premium Christmas stollen also had an award-based quality signal and fits the firm's festive specialty identity, so management would be inclined to keep it unless results turned clearly negative.
